title: With AI, Sharing Is Caring
gist: Jeff Jarvis argues that public distrust of Big Tech should not lead to starving AI models of the data and authoritative information they need. If privacy and copyright advocates and regulators cut off or poison AI's data sources, the result will be bad AI; everyone relying on AI output has a duty to supply high-quality input.

insights.claim: Jarvis argues that distrust of Big Tech, while understandable, is not a reason to starve AI models of the information and data they need to be useful.
insights.speaker: JEFF JARVIS
insights.so_what: Represents a pro-access counterweight in the training-data licensing and copyright debate affecting AI developers.

insights.claim: Jarvis warns that if privacy and copyright advocates, regulators, and AI critics succeed in cutting off or poisoning AI's sources of reliable data, the result will be worse AI.
insights.speaker: JEFF JARVIS
insights.so_what: Restrictive data regimes could degrade model quality and shift advantage to firms with proprietary data.
insights.quote: If privacy and copyright advocates, regulators, and crusaders against the technology succeed in cutting off or poisoning AI’s sources of reliable data and authoritative information, won’t bad AI be the result?

insights.claim: Jarvis contends that if serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on AI's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.
insights.speaker: JEFF JARVIS
insights.so_what: Supports arguments for publishers and institutions to license or open data to AI, potentially creating new data-licensing markets.
